title: El Calafate: glaciers and lakes in Patagonia
meta_description: El Calafate guide: Perito Moreno Glacier, boat trips on Lake Argentino, things to do, how to get there and where to stay.
hero_subtitle: The gateway to Perito Moreno Glacier, on the shores of Lake Argentino.

why_visit.title: Perito Moreno
why_visit.text: One of the most accessible glaciers in the world: from the walkways you see it face to face and hear the ice break off.

why_visit.title: World Heritage Site
why_visit.text: Los Glaciares National Park is recognized by UNESCO for its ice fields and glaciers.

why_visit.title: Lakes and icebergs
why_visit.text: Boat trips on Lake Argentino reach other glaciers and sail among icebergs of incredible colors.

why_visit.title: Base for El Chaltén
why_visit.text: From El Calafate you can continue by road to El Chaltén, the trekking capital.

activities.title: Perito Moreno walkways
activities.text: Several kilometers of trails facing the glacier, with balconies at different heights. Stay a while in one spot to watch the ice calve.

activities.title: Walking on the ice
activities.text: Crampon hikes on the glacier, always with licensed guides. Spots and age limits apply, and they sell out in high season.

activities.title: Boat trips on Lake Argentino
activities.text: Boat trips in front of Perito Moreno and longer excursions to other glaciers in the park, such as Upsala and Spegazzini.

activities.title: Laguna Nimez Reserve
activities.text: Steps from downtown, a trail through wetlands where you can see flamingos, black-necked swans and many other birds.

activities.title: Glaciarium
activities.text: An interpretation center dedicated to glaciers, ideal for understanding what you'll see in the park.

how_to_get_there:
By plane: El Calafate International Airport (FTE) has direct flights from Buenos Aires, about 3 hours, and connections with other cities. It's about 20 km from town.

Overland: there are buses from Río Gallegos, from El Chaltén (about 220 km away) and from Puerto Natales, Chile.

To the glacier: Perito Moreno is about 80 km away on a paved road. Go on a tour, by scheduled bus or by car.

where_to_stay.budget: Hostels with shared rooms and guest kitchens, plus campsites in season. They're the most affordable option and a good place to meet other travelers.
where_to_stay.midrange: Inns, cabins and small hotels, often with breakfast included. Cabins with kitchens suit families and groups.
where_to_stay.luxury: Upscale hotels and lodges with landscape views, spas or tours included. Book them well in advance.

practical_tips.title: Best time
practical_tips.text: From October to April all tours run and days are long. The park is open all year.

practical_tips.title: Changeable weather
practical_tips.text: Wind and sudden weather changes are part of the trip. Dress in layers and always carry a windbreaker.

practical_tips.title: Book ahead
practical_tips.text: In high season, lodging and tours fill up. It's best to book as soon as you have your dates.

practical_tips.title: Prices and payments
practical_tips.text: Prices change often: check current rates before you travel and carry some cash as well as cards.

closing: Set aside at least one full day for Perito Moreno and another for the lake. And if you can, continue on to El Chaltén.
